spec: Task 005 stage 1: generate(mesocycle, cycle_one) -> microcycles 2..N, every one stamped with ENGINE_VERSION. Dates are ISO here and whole days since 1970-01-01 in the core; each consumer converts. An expected load is target_weight_kg when it is an exact decimal, or target_weight_steps (x the exercise's increment, in the consumer's own arithmetic) when it is not. The output is compared whole: every cycle, session, exercise and set, in canonical order.

cases.name: fixture #1 — the owner's example: 40 kg 3x6 to 62.5 kg at cycle 11, deloads at 6 and 12
cases.note: 00 § Worked example. A deload consumes no step: cycle 7 resumes one step past cycle 5. It prescribes the last working load x 6000 bp (50 -> 30, 62.5 -> 37.5), 3 sets x 5000 bp with a tie to the fewer (1 set), and RIR 3 + 2 = 5 clamped to the rule's 4 and marked (01 FR-3.9).

cases.name: a block of 9-day microcycles: cycle 3 starts 18 days after cycle 1
cases.note: INV-25. 2026-10-05, 2026-10-14, 2026-10-23: no weekday anywhere. Three sessions on days 1, 4 and 7 keep their day indices in every cycle.

cases.name: mostly 7-day cycles with one 5-day cycle: every later start shifts, and day 7's session moves to day 5
cases.note: FR-3.1a, INV-25. Starts 10-05, 10-12, 10-19, then 10-24 — five days later, not seven. A session past the end of the shorter cycle moves to its last day, after the session already there (order 1): nothing is dropped. Loads tell the sessions apart.

cases.name: 24 cycles with deload_mode none: 24 working cycles and no deload anywhere
cases.note: FR-3.1b: 'none' is a first-class choice. 40 kg + 2.5 kg a cycle reaches 97.5 kg at cycle 24.

cases.name: a 2.5 % step (load_step_bp = 250) from a 140 kg squat prescribes 142.5 kg
cases.note: ADR-010 §3. A share of cycle 1's load per step, never compounded: 143.5 -> 142.5, 147 -> 147.5 (a tie would go lighter; 147 is 58.8 steps, nearer 59), 150.5 -> 150. The former 3 % gave 145.

cases.name: every second cycle a deload, and the final cycle too
cases.note: FR-3.1b. Deloads at 2 and 4, and 5 because final_cycle is set and the beat misses it. Cycle 3 is one step past cycle 1 (105). A deload multiplies the last working cycle: 100 x 0.6 = 60; 105 x 0.6 = 63 -> 62.5, for cycle 4 and for cycle 5. Two working sets deload to one. No RIR target stays none (INV-03).

cases.name: a manual deload on a fixed exercise keeps the warm-up and half the working sets
cases.note: FR-3.5, FR-3.9. Fixed holds 60 kg; the deload is the cycle's, so it applies. Four working sets keep two; the warm-up is not a counted set, so it stays, deloaded like the rest: 20 x 0.6 = 12 -> 12.5; 60 x 0.6 = 36 -> 35. RIR 2 + 2 = 4 fits the rule, so nothing is clamped.

cases.name: a target carried from cycle 1 outside its rule is clamped into it and marked
cases.note: INV-05: the engine never generates a set outside its rule. 10 reps on a 6-8 rule is 8; RIR 6 with a maximum of 4 is 4; was_clamped says why. Cycle 1 itself is the user's and is not rewritten.

cases.name: an imperial block stays on the 5 lb grid: 135 lb + 5 lb a cycle
cases.note: ADR-008, INV-02. 5 lb is stored as 2.267962 kg (numeric(10,6)) and 135 lb as 61.235 kg (numeric(9,4)). Expected loads are whole steps of the increment — 28, 29, 30, i.e. 140, 145 and 150 lb — written as steps because a product of 2.267962 has no short exact decimal.
